title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.
summary: This paper proves the existence of the Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals, showing that wave localization occurs at specific momentum values (mobility edges) rather than just at critical modulation strengths. By extending established concepts from spatial lattices to the time domain, it offers deep insights into wave propagation control in time-varying photonic structures.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and nature of the Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals, extending the concept from spatial lattices to the time domain.
main_result: The Aubry-André transition is confirmed to exist in these time-modulated photonic systems, occurring at mobility edges in momentum space rather than in energy.
method: The analysis employs transfer matrix methods, utilizing Avila's global theory and calculating the Lyapunov exponent (growth rate) across different modulation strengths and wave numbers.
model_or_system: The system models light propagation in photonic time quasicrystals, where the permittivity is modulated periodically in time. The dynamics are governed by an equation related to the almost-Mathieu equation, analyzed via a transfer matrix approach.

important_parameters: Modulation strength ($\lambda$), wave number ($k$), and the ratio of modulation contrast ($r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the impulsive modulation limit (exact reduction to the Aubry-André model) and the use of Avila's theory for general analytic modulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition using wave-packet intensity and growth rate vs. modulation strength, showing mobility edges in momentum space, and comparing power spectra for delocalized, gap, and localized wave numbers.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical analogy to the Aubry-André model, derives the governing equations, and then uses advanced mathematical tools (Avila's theory, Lyapunov exponents) to pinpoint the transition mechanism, showing it manifests as a momentum-dependent mobility edge.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from solid-state physics (Anderson/Aubry-André localization) into the time domain of photonics, providing a powerful tool for understanding wave transport in engineered time-varying media.
